---
title: "Part 3 – Reproduction and the specification menu"
---
::: {.callout-note appearance="simple" icon=false}
**Slides.** [Open the deck at this part](../../slides/one-day-methods.html#/part-3-reproduce-then-take-the-model-apart){target="_blank"} in its own tab, or follow it on the [slides page](slides.qmd).
:::

Part 3 begins with the reproduction, then takes the menu apart axis by axis to show what each choice does to an estimate, and ends with a round of exploration of your own.

| Work through | What you do | Timing |
|---|---|---|
| Slides, the constrained task | The three Multi100 instructions read verbatim, what each assumes, the columns of the panel, and the aim of the reproduction. | 10 minutes |
| Your working script, or [Browser lab](../../exercise/browser-lab.qmd) Task 3 | Fit `mcosmo ~ unemp_c` with country and year fixed effects, which should give t = −3.804 (df = 233, N = 270), the value recorded by Multi100 for analyst C6HJR. Type your t without sending it, and send it when the facilitator says go. Then the question of why everyone in the class got the same t while five analysts, each writing their own code, did not. | 20 minutes |
| [Specification menu](../../exercise/spec-menu.qmd) and slides | The fourteen decisions, the three levels into which they sort, the options that the curve of 864 keeps, what Task 2 of Multi100 left open, the ground rules for the menu and the claim-alignment convention that puts every result on one scale. | 15 minutes |
| Slides, the methodological tutorial, with [The statistical methods behind the course](../../companion/stats-methods.qmd) as the companion | Nine of the fourteen decisions, a slide or two each: the six framing scales; building a scale from a mean, sum or share; claim alignment; a bounded scale in a linear model; the predictor, unemployment or GDP growth; predictor form; the estimators for countries and years, and what fixed effects adjust for; the copredictor; sample restrictions; weights; and making the axes comparable. | 25 minutes |
| Task 4 in the workspace or on the [Browser lab](../../exercise/browser-lab.qmd), then [Multiverse](../../results.qmd) | Call `try_spec()` three or four times, changing one argument at a time, print them with `my_experiments()`, then submit the one you would defend with `submit_exploration()`. Your dot is drawn on the chart as an open circle. | 20 minutes |

**By the end of the part** you have reproduced t = −3.804, you can say what each decision of the menu does to an estimate, and you have an exploratory dot on the class chart.
